info.bio: Biohazard es una banda de hardcore punk formada en el año 1988 en el distrito newyorquino de Brooklyn. Integraban la formación original el guitarrista/vocalista Billy Graziadei, el bajista/vocalista Evan Seinfeld, el guitarrista Bobby Hambel, y el baterista Danny Shuler. Ellos formaron Biohazard con el propósito de expresar puntos de vista políticos, y para discutir los problemas que enfrentaba la juventud urbana. Influenciados por bandas como Black Sabbath

scenes.name: Metal agresivo: Pantera y el metalcore
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Las excepciones a la muerte del metal no son lite metal: cambian el poder del heavy por la agresión. Pantera debuta en una multinacional con Cowboys from Hell (1990), que ni entra en los 200; sin radio y con poca presencia en Headbangers Ball, a base de giras, Far Beyond Driven llega al número uno en 1994. Ese año Slayer coloca Divine Intervention en el top ten. Del cruce entre thrash y hardcore sale el llamado metalcore, con voces entrecortadas y poca melodía: Pantera, Biohazard y Machine Head.

scenes.name: Metal de los noventa: progresivo, death y black metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Si los ochenta fueron la edad de oro del heavy metal, los noventa lo fragmentan en estilos que amplían ideas anteriores. El pop-metal (Warrant, Extreme, Live) es lo menos significativo; Marilyn Manson casa el scum-rock de Alice Cooper con el industrial de Nine Inch Nails. El metal progresivo (Warrior Soul, Dream Theater, Royal Hunt, Opeth, los suizos Alboth!). El death metal muta en algo más terrible y más musical gracias a Brutal Truth, Cannibal Corpse y, sobre todo, la tríada de Type O Negative (Slow Deep And Hard, misas negras wagnerianas), Today Is The Day y Fear Factory; Biohazard, Coalesce, Dillinger Escape Plan. El nuevo black metal escandinavo: Entombed, Darkthrone, Immortal, Mayhem, Enslaved, Emperor, Satyricon, Cradle Of Filth.

podcast.title: Comeback in Alternative Metal
podcast.body: Biohazard was mentioned as an older group that made a comeback in the 2010s, alongside Jane's Addiction and Faith No More, within the Alternative Metal/Alternative Hard Rock scene that was prominent in the 90s. This contributed to the renewed success of heavy bands from the past. "Plus we saw comebacks from older groups like Jane's Addiction, Biohazard and Faith No More to name a few."

xref.title: Porn Production Company and Website (Unspecified Years)
xref.body: Evan Seinfeld, former singer for Biohazard, founded a porn production company called Tara Vision with his wife, adult film star Tara Patrick. He directed and performed with her in seven films and also operated the website rockstarpornstar.com. Seinfeld stated that he earned more money in three years in the porn industry than in 20 years in music. While no longer actively performing, he remained involved behind the scenes, including with Is My Girl, a website enabling models to produce and sell their own content, which served as a precursor to OnlyFans. "Evan said he made more money in the three years in the porn business that he did in 20 years playing music."
